subject: Post-call: VPC & air-gapped hosting priorities (Medicore)
messages:
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Sanjeev Rao <sanjeev@medicore.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: VPC & air-gapped hosting priorities (Medicore)

Hi Sanjeev — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap of the items we captured and the suggested next steps so we keep momentum on the POC planning. Please correct any misunderstandings.

Summary of your pain & goals
- Data residency: PHI must remain in US-only regions and be logically segregated from other tenants.
- Network isolation: primary requirement is an air-gapped or strictly outbound-only deployment model for production inference; no inbound internet traffic to inference nodes.
- Audit & retention: 3+ years of immutable audit logs for inference requests and access events.
- Key management: customer-controlled KMS/HSM integration for encryption at rest and in-flight key wrapping.
- Model lifecycle: ability to ship model updates offline (manual signing/airlift) without exposing artifacts to public networks.

Success criteria for POC
- Demonstrate inference within your VPC with egress-only flow and no inbound open ports to model nodes.
- Show KMS/HSM integration for one test model and end-to-end encryption of logs.
- Latency: 95th percentile under 300ms for your clinical triage workload under sample traffic shape.
- Cost telemetry and per-token cost estimate for projected monthly volume.

Open constraints we captured
- Your security team prefers an air-gap approach for production; dev/test may be less restrictive.
- There are existing on-prem SAML auth systems and an internal time-limited key distribution process for deploys.
- The network team requires minimal CIDR exposure and explicit allowlists for egress destinations (monitoring, updates).

Next steps (owner / ETA)
- We will send our VPC & connectivity requirements doc and a template network diagram (attached) — Monica / today.
- Medicore to share a high-level network diagram showing firewall/egress controls and KMS/HSM provider details — Sanjeev / by 2027-04-23.
- Schedule a technical deep-dive with your infra + security (Ben + Lauren to join) to validate ports, egress endpoints, and maintenance/update process — Monica / propose times this week.
- Redwood to draft a PO/estimated cost range for the POC (ballpark) — Monica / by next Tue.

Attachments: Redwood_VPC_Requirements_v1.pdf (link included), Medicore_PHI_Map.xlsx (we referenced a template that may help map data flows).

Thanks again — I’ll follow up with a calendar invite for the deep-dive.

Best,
Monica Patel
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Sanjeev Rao <sanjeev@medicore.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Medicore Infrastructure Team <infra@medicore.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 09:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: VPC & air-gapped hosting priorities (Medicore)

Thanks Monica — helpful summary. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Correct on PHI residency and air-gap requirement for production. For initial POC we can allow a controlled egress path to Redwood monitoring/metrics endpoints only.
- KMS/HSM: we currently use Thales Luna for HSM. We need to confirm whether Redwood can integrate with on-prem HSM via a broker or if you require cloud KMS.
- Offline model updates: our change control requires signed artifacts and an offline push mechanism by our release engineering team. Can you describe your suggested workflow for signed model artifacts?
- Ports/endpoints: security will publish a list but expect that only a handful of outbound destinations are allowed (no DNS-based dynamic egress rules).

Can you also provide a simple example network diagram template we can drop our IPs into? That will make the security review faster.

If possible, please include a ballpark monthly cost range for the POC (reserved capacity + transfer/ingest) — we understand it will be approximate.

On timing: we aim to have a completed security review and an internal approval by the end of May, so a technical deep-dive early next week would be ideal.

Thanks — Sanjeev
Sanjeev Rao
Head of Infrastructure | Medicore Health
sanjeev@medicore.com
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Sanjeev Rao <sanjeev@medicore.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 09:14:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: VPC & air-gapped hosting priorities (Medicore)

Appreciate the fast reply, Sanjeev. Short answers inline below and next actions.

> Can you provide a simple example network diagram template?
Yes — attaching a one-page template (Redwood_VPC_Requirements_v1.pdf) and a spreadsheet to map PHI zones (Medicore_PHI_Map.xlsx). Use the template to drop in your CIDRs and we’ll iterate.

> HSM integration with Thales Luna
We support two approaches: 1) Brokered HSM integration via a customer-managed gateway that we can talk to over an egress-only connection, or 2) use your cloud KMS for key wrapping and keep master keys in your on-prem HSM. Both are commonly used; Ben will follow up with specifics and a short security note on supported key wrap protocols.

> Offline signed model deploys
Our recommended flow for air-gap: sign model artifacts with your release-signing key, SFTP/airlift the artifact into the isolated subnet, and we run verification scripts inside the VPC. We can provide the verification tooling and a small ops runbook for your release team.

> Cost ballpark for POC
For the scope we discussed (single-model, reserved capacity for 6-8 vCPU-equivalent GPU baseline, limited egress), estimated monthly range: $12k–$25k depending on commit level and telemetry retention. We’ll put a clearer line-item estimate in the PO draft.

Next actions (updated)
- Monica: send meeting invite for technical deep-dive — proposing Mon 2027-04-26 10:00am PT / alternative Wed 2027-04-28 2:00pm PT.
- Sanjeev: drop your high-level network diagram and HSM contact details into the attached template — by 2027-04-23.
- Ben: provide HSM/KMS integration note and key-wrap protocol options ahead of the deep-dive.

If their schedule works, I’ll lock the Mon timeslot. Thanks again — looking forward to the deep-dive.

Best,
Monica
